reviewMethod: Independent visual reading of all 24 question-paper pages and PDF pages 23–44 of the combined Higher Level scheme (the Paper 2 title page 23, the scale table on page 24, the summary of mark allocations on page 25, every Paper 2 model solution and marking note on pages 26–43, and the back cover on page 44). Each task boundary is the published scale beside its model solution, cross-checked against the printed summary.
sourceNotes: The paper is 300 marks: candidates answer all nine questions (Section A Q1–6, 25 marks each; Section B Q7 50 marks, Q8 60 marks, Q9 40 marks). Every question is retained.
32 independently marked units, matching the printed summary of allocations on scheme page 25. Q8(b)(ii) and (iii) share one 10D scale (“(b)(ii)+(iii)”) and are one task.

Paper 2 bands from the scale table on scheme page 24 (headed “Paper 1” in print, but it is the Paper 2 table and its ladders differ from Paper 1’s): 5B 0,2,5; 5C 0,2,4,5; 10C 0,3,7,10; 10D 0,3,5,8,10; 15C 0,4,11,15; 15D 0,4,7,11,15; 20C 0,7,13,20; 20D 0,5,10,15,20. Every part prints the same ladder beside its scale.

This paper had no authored cards before this review; all 32 units are new. Marking points are lifted line by line from the scheme (read through the glyph repair map) and labelled with the part of the scheme they come from; Q1(b), Q5(b) and Q5(c) keep each printed method’s ladder separately, and a few long methods are quoted as one multi-line point to stay within the row limit. The Q8(b)(i) tick table is quoted statement by statement with the ticked column in the label.

Six parts carry the SEC’s own print of their scheme row (model solution and every credit band), cropped from the scheme PDF and shown only after the reveal, because the working refers to a diagram or graph, a tick table, or a line whose stacked-fraction digits extract as lone numerals: Q4(b), Q6(a), Q7(d), Q8(b)(i), Q8(c), Q9(b)(iii).

The question booklet is LC003ALP200EV.pdf; its indexed scheme LC003ALP000EV.pdf is shared with Paper 1. Scheme page references are PDF positions (printed page number + 3); question-paper PDF positions match the printed page numbers.

cards.stem: In a competition Mary has a probability of 1/20 of winning, a probability of 1/10 of finishing in second place, and a probability of 1/4 of finishing in third place. If she wins the competition she gets €9000. If she comes second she gets €7000 and if she comes third she gets €3000. In all other cases she gets nothing. Each participant in the competition must pay €2000 to enter.
cards.questionText: Find the expected value of Mary’s loss if she enters the competition.

cards.questionText: Acme Confectionery has an employee pension plan. For an employee who qualifies for the full pension, Acme Confectionery will pay a sum of €20 000 on the day of retirement. It will then pay a sum on the same date each subsequent year for the next 25 years. Each year the employee is paid a sum that is 1% more than the amount paid in the previous year. What sum of money must the company have set aside on the day of retirement in order to fund this pension? Assume an annual interest rate (AER) of 2·4%.
